nodes.label: Pairing and Login Setup Flow
nodes.rationale: Pairing and login are deliberately separate: pairing sends no username or password and does not log in, and login authorizes filesystem operations for one QUIC connection only. Trust records are keyed by both --server and --server-name, so both must match between pairing and later use.

nodes.label: Split of Server, Client, and Export State
nodes.rationale: Server state (TLS key, Argon2id hashes, pairing records) must never be copied to clients; the export root must stay disjoint from it so authenticated filesystem clients cannot reach secrets.

nodes.label: Rust 1.88 / Edition 2024 Prerequisite
nodes.rationale: Rust 1.85 first stabilized edition 2024, but the dependency graph raises the supported minimum to 1.88; distribution Cargo packages are frequently too old, so rustup-managed stable is required for rust-toolchain.toml to be honored.

nodes.label: macFUSE Installation Preflight
nodes.rationale: Every macOS client process checks for the macFUSE bundle at startup and exits with the installation link; quicKFS deliberately does not install, approve, or update the system extension. The check is repeated per launch so there is no cached result to clear.

nodes.label: Enterprise Setup Without Per-Client Pairing
nodes.rationale: QuickFS parses the chain and verifies leaf/key match and QUIC/TLS usability, but clients remain the authority for lifetime, name, and CA-chain validation. The staging key stays outside QuickFS state and must be retired by the organization's secret-delivery policy.
